## Claims
- [source-backed] Native arXiv source identity: Avery St. Dizier and Alexander Yong, *Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture*, arXiv:2209.02011v2, DOI 10.1112/jlms.12832. The source title, authors, and abstract are present. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 114-131]
- [source-backed] Definition 2.1 defines a valid tuple \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) by \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\), \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), and \(N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]
- [source-backed] Equations (8)–(10) in the native source are respectively the definition of \(\mathrm{CP}\), the algorithm update \(\xi^{(m)}=\xi^{(m-1)}-\gamma\mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes\prod_p\overline{s}_{\mu^{(p)}})\), and the system \(\{\linear_\varphi(\nu)=d_\nu\mid\nu\in\decomp_\varphi\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 387-397] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 625-632] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-798]
- [source-backed] Lemma 2.5 states that a nonzero homogeneous syzygy yields consistency of the decomposable equations, with right side \(f_{\nu_B}\) for tall \(\nu\) and \(0\) for wide \(\nu\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 326-344]
- [source-backed] The formal item numbered 4.4 is a **Proposition**, not a theorem: for tall nonempty \(\nu\), \(\mathrm{Reduce}_{\varphi}(\nu)=(-1)^{|\nu_B|+1}(1\otimes\overline{s}_{(\nu_B)'})\). The formal item numbered 4.5 is a **Lemma**, not a theorem: \(\sum_{\lambda,\mu}(-1)^{|\lambda|}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\nu}s_{\lambda'}s_\mu=0\) for \(\nu\ne\varnothing\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 667-705]
